name: Collage
traits: cut-out photographs layered with flat coloured paper
visible scissor edges, tape and glue shadows
mixed textures: newsprint grain, halftone, kraft paper
bestFor: brands that want a zine or scrapbook voice
suits: fashion, beauty, music, snacks, lifestyle and youth products; bold, playful, creative brands
stylePara: Cut-and-paste collage animation: characters and props are cut from black-and-white and faded colour photographs and combined with flat shapes of coloured paper, kraft card and halftone printed scraps; pieces overlap at mismatched scales and slight angles, with white scissor borders, torn edges, strips of matte tape and small drop shadows where they lift off the board; textures mix newsprint grain, coarse halftone and paper fibre; a limited accent palette of one hot colour plus the paper tones; everything sits on a flat board lit evenly from above.

rendering.line: no drawn lines; shapes are defined by scissor cuts with a thin white border or a torn fibre edge
rendering.shading: photographic shading inside each cut-out, plus small drop shadows under lifted pieces; no global lighting
rendering.colour: desaturated photo pieces and paper neutrals with one hot accent colour; the product cut-out kept in its exact green and yellow as the brightest piece
rendering.texture: newsprint grain, halftone dots, kraft paper, tape, glue wrinkles, slight curling
rendering.lighting: flat even top light over the board; shadows only where pieces lift

motion: Stop-motion cut-out on twos and threes: pieces pop on and off in single frames, slide and rotate as flat cards, and replace each other in quick swaps; heads and hands are swapped cut-outs rather than animated; a few pieces tremble slightly between frames as if re-placed by hand.
camera: Top-down rostrum camera over the board; quick push-ins and snap zooms; pieces enter from off-frame; no 3D camera moves around the pieces.
avoid: seamless photoreal compositing with matched lighting
a woman whose cut-out face changes between shots
magazine headlines and printed words on the scraps
sheets: The woman as one consistent set of photo cut-outs (head front, head three-quarter, body, two hand poses) with the same white border, so the face is reused, not re-invented; the place as a collage board with its paper pieces; the product as a clean cut-out of its exact bottle.
risk: Seedance tends to blend the pieces into one photoreal composite and to fill newsprint scraps with garbled headlines; say 'separate flat cut-outs with white borders, no blending' and 'the newsprint is texture only, no readable words'. The photographed face is the identity risk; reuse the same cut-out head from the sheet and keep her face small or in profile.

example.prompt: Cut-and-paste collage still on a flat board: a woman in her thirties with a dark bun cut from a black-and-white photograph, her orange top cut from flat orange paper, holds a bright cut-out of a small green glass bottle with a yellow cap; a sunny kitchen assembled from faded photo scraps and kraft card at mismatched scales, a droopy fern from a halftone print on the windowsill; white scissor borders, torn edges, tape strips, small drop shadows. Vertical 9:16. No text.
